text: Uncle Oscar Cresswell, the mothers brother, found Paul riding one day and learned that the boy had named his rocking horse Sansovino after the horse that had won at Ascot. <break time="0.8s" /> Surprised, the uncle discovered that Paul knew a great deal about racing from Bassett, the young gardener, who had been wounded in the war and had once served as Oscars batman. <break time="0.8s" /> When Pauls tip, Daffodil, came in first at the Lincoln race, the astonished uncle learned that the boy and Bassett were secret partners and that Paul now had fifteen hundred pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Bassett, speaking as if he were talking about religious matters, explained that Master Paul seemed to get his tips from heaven and that they never lost when Paul was quite sure. <break time="0.8s" /> So Uncle Oscar became a third partner, and when Paul was sure about Lively Spark, a quite inconsiderable horse, the uncle won two thousand pounds, while the boy himself won ten thousand. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Paul revealed why he wanted money, explaining, I started it for mother, because she said she had no luck, and I thought that if I was lucky, it might stop whispering. <break time="0.8s" /> What might stop whispering, asked the uncle, and the boy, who seemed nervous, said in a low voice, Our house, I hate our house for whispering. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy did not want his mother to know that he was lucky, saying, She would stop me, and so the two began to plan how to give her money in secret.
